title: Clinical study of the anesthetic efficacy of 2% lidocaine gel versus tetracaine/oxybuprocaine anesthetic eye drops in patients operated on for glaucoma and undergoing needing techniques in outpatient surgery
official: Clinical study of the anesthetic efficacy of 2% lidocaine gel versus tetracaine/oxybuprocaine anesthetic eye drops in patients operated on for glaucoma and undergoing needing techniques in outpatient surgery
summary:
Main objective: To compare the anaesthetic efficacy of 2% lidocaine gel with 0.1% hydrochloride tetracaine eye drops / 0.4% oxybuprocaine hydrochloride in the in-office needling procedure in glaucoma surgery patients.
To determine the mean procedure time in both anaesthetic treatment arms.

interventions.name: Ophtesic 20 mg/g, gel oftálmico en envase unidosis
COLIROFTA ANESTÉSICO DOBLE 1 MG/ML + 4 MG/ML COLIRIO EN SOLUCIÓN

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients operated on glaucoma surgery with filter blister who require the needling procedure
2. Patients over 18 years of age, who have understood and signed the informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnant or lactating patients.
2. Patients with cognitive impairment who do not understand the visual analogue scale.
3. Hearing loss that prevents the patient from collaborating
4. Anxiety disorder that prevents patient's collaboration during the procedure
5. Allergy to topical anesthetics
6. Patients who require needling in the operating room
